newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan harvests 25 pct of crop vs 35 pct avg.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan harvests 25 pct of crop vs 35 pct avg.

text.p: Saskatchewan harvested 25 percent of all crops through the week ended September 9, compared to the five-year average of 35 percent, according to Saskatchewan Agriculture.
Grade quality was above average across the grainbelt with 87 percent of the harvest spring wheat grading number one, 11 percent number two, and two percent number three.
The 10-year average for spring wheat has 47 percent at No1, 24 percent at No2, 19 percent at No3 and 10 percent feed.
An average 20 mm (0.8 inch) of rain halted harvest last week until warmer, drier weather returned by the weekend.

Southern Saskatchewan saw an average 17 mm of rain. A light frost was reported in Avonlea Friday morning. Ergot was reported in wheat in the Estevan and Regina regions. Sawfly and Bertha armyworms were reported in the Assiniboia region.

Central Saskatchewan saw an average 20 mm of rain. Light frost was reported in the Ituna, Endeavour, Kelvington, Rosetown and Ruthilda areas. Bertha armyworms caused damage to canola around the Melville and Watrous regions. Blackleg and take all root rot caused damage in canola around Canora, Saskatoon.
Northern Saskatchewan saw an average 16 mm of rain. Frost struck Tisdale, St. Brieux, Beatty, Henribourg, and Spiritwood.
Ergot was reported in wheat around North Battleford. Sclerotinia was found in canola around Tisdale and green aphid damage was found on crops around Humboldt.
